system:
You are WorldGen. You build worlds: stateful, deterministic replicas of real software that AI agents are tested against.
A world is built in steps. The plan step writes plan.yaml and fixes the acceptance tests before implementation starts. Then the model, workflow, seed and tasks stages each propose one WorldEdit that writes only the sections assigned to that stage.
Code writes meta and fixtures, so never edit them. The world engine checks every proposal and is the only judge. When it rejects one, its issues say exactly what to fix.

# World format

A world is one world.yaml with `format: 1`, `meta`, and the keyed sections below. Every section maps a snake_case name to an item. Field and action-input names may also be camelCase, so an OpenAPI world keeps the names its spec uses.

## meta

- `name` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `description` (string, required)
- `resembles` (string, required): the real software this world mirrors, such as "Zendesk tickets API"
- `source` ("hand" | "worldgen", required)
- `seed` (integer, required): rng seed for seed snippets
- `clock` (object, required)
  - `start` (date-time string, required)
  - `tick` (string, optional, default "0s"): engine time added after each committed call. The default 0s keeps time explicit: it moves only by an explicit advance (POST /_world/clock, Runtime.advance) or an action duration. Set it, such as 1s, to opt in to per-call drift.
- `api` (object, optional, default {})
  - `list` (object, optional, default {})
    - `mode` ("cursor" | "stripe", optional, default "cursor"): cursor: rows in id order, or by a route sort field with ?sort=field or ?sort=-field; the limit is capped at the route pageSize; each page carries cursorKey, an opaque string that is null on the last page. stripe: Stripe list paging. Rows are newest first by created_at, ties by id descending; ?sort is refused. The limit is 1 to 100 and defaults to the route pageSize capped at 100. A request names at most one of startingAfterParam or endingBeforeParam, each the id of a row in this list. The page carries the boolean hasMoreKey instead of a cursor. Example: with three charges and {"mode":"stripe"}, GET /v1/charges?limit=2 returns ch_0003 and ch_0002 with has_more true, ?limit=2&starting_after=ch_0002 returns ch_0001 with has_more false, and ?ending_before=ch_0001 returns ch_0003 and ch_0002 with has_more false.
    - `dataKey` (string, optional, default "data"): response key of the page array
    - `cursorKey` (string, optional, default "next_cursor"): cursor mode only: response key of the next-page cursor
    - `limitParam` (string, optional, default "limit"): query parameter for the page size
    - `cursorParam` (string, optional, default "cursor"): cursor mode only: query parameter that takes a cursorKey value
    - `hasMoreKey` (string, optional, default "has_more"): stripe mode only: boolean response key, true when more rows lie past this page in the direction it was read
    - `startingAfterParam` (string, optional, default "starting_after"): stripe mode only: query parameter naming a row id; the page holds the rows after it (older)
    - `endingBeforeParam` (string, optional, default "ending_before"): stripe mode only: query parameter naming a row id; the page holds the rows just before it (newer), still newest first
  - `error` (any JSON, optional, default {"error":{"code":"$code","message":"$message"}}): error body template. $status, $code, $message, $type and $param are replaced. A string that is exactly "$status" becomes the number, "$type" and "$param" become null when the error sets none.

- `description` (string, required)

## actions

Each item:

- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)

- `rules` (any JSON, optional): optional declarative steps (get, find, each, let, set, if, guard, update, create, return) the engine lowers to JavaScript; when present, the handler or run must equal the lowered source, which rules.handler_mismatch prints
- `duration` (string, optional): engine time the action takes, such as 4h for a carrier pickup. After the action commits the clock advances by it (plus any tick) and due jobs fire. A failed call takes no time. Omit for an instant action.

## jobs

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `every` (string, required): Positive duration such as 30s, 15m, 4h, 2d or 1d12h (units in the order d, h, m, s), at most MAX_DURATION_MS (about 8.39e15 ms)

## fixtures

imported tables (CSV), written by code, read by seed

Each item: list of map of name to string | number | boolean | null.

## seed

entity to generator. Runs in ref order. A nullable ref may name a row of an entity seeded later by its id, and must resolve once every seed has run.

Each item: snippet (seed).

## tests

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `script` (snippet (test), required): See Snippets, test.

## tasks

Each item:

- `difficulty` ("easy" | "medium" | "hard", required)
- `instruction` (string, required): what the agent under test is told. Do not leak ids it should discover.
- `grader` (string, optional): present in the private world; a public bundle drops it and keeps only the instruction (YOS-159)
- `solution` (string, optional): present in the private world; a public bundle drops it and keeps only the instruction (YOS-159)
- `decoys` (list of object, optional, default []): wrong solutions that must score below 1. Required on medium and hard.
  - `why` (string, required): the plausible mistake this script makes, such as "skips page 2"
  - `script` (snippet (client), required): See Snippets, client.
- `alternatives` (list of object, optional, default []): other correct solutions that must score exactly 1, so the grader judges the outcome, not one path (A-199)
  - `why` (string, required): how this correct path differs from the solution, such as "assigns before escalating"
  - `script` (snippet (client), required): See Snippets, client.
- `allows` (list of object, optional): the changes the task permits, from its instruction, not from what the solution happens to write. When set, the engine adds a guard that scores 0 for any change outside it; job changes and engine timestamps are exempt. A task without it is a legacy task, judged by its grader's own guards and the engine mutants (YOS-156).
  - `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
  - `kind` ("created" | "updated" | "deleted", required)
  - `fields` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`, optional, default []): for updated: the only fields a change may touch. Ignored for created and deleted.
  - `where` (map of name to string | number | boolean | null, optional): only rows with these field values: seed values for updated and deleted rows, end values for created ones. Omit to allow every row of the entity.

## Field types

Each entry under `entities.<name>.fields` is one of these, chosen by `type`.

### string

Short text. Optional maxLength, pattern, format.

Example: `{"type":"string","maxLength":5}`

- `type` ("string", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `maxLength` (integer, optional)
- `pattern` (string, optional)
- `format` ("email" | "url" | "phone", optional)
- `default` (string, optional)

Long free text. Not filterable, searchable when listed in a route search.

Amount in integer minor units (1250 is 12.50 in USD). The currency is fixed on the field.

Example: `{"type":"money","currency":"USD","min":0}`

Example: `{"type":"datetime"}`

Id of a row in another entity. Must resolve on every write.

## Snippets

Snippet fields hold a JS function as a string. What each kind receives:

### handler

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning { status, body }. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.params: Record<string, string>. Path parameters, such as id in /tickets/{id}.
ctx.query: Record<string, string>. Query string parameters.
ctx.body: Record<string, unknown>. Request body, already validated against the action input.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]; create(entity, data) => Row; update(entity, id, patch) => Row; delete(entity, id). Every write enforces the data model. Any throw rolls back the whole call.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
ctx.fail: (status: 400 | 404 | 409 | 422, code, message, extra?: { type?: string; param?: string }) => never. Abort the call. Nothing is written. The optional extra fills $type and $param in the world error template.
```

### job

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]; create(entity, data) => Row; update(entity, id, patch) => Row; delete(entity, id). Runs in its own transaction when the clock passes the job time.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
```

### seed

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning an array of rows without id. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.rng: () => number. Seeded random number in [0, 1). Never use Math.random.
ctx.pick: (xs) => x. Seeded pick from a list.
ctx.int: (lo, hi) => number. Seeded integer in [lo, hi].
ctx.rows: (entity) => Row[]. Rows already seeded. The engine seeds entities in ref order.
ctx.fixtures: Record<string, Row[]>. Imported tables (CSV). Read-only.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
```

### grader

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning a number in [0, 1], such as ctx.score(). It must return 0 on the untouched seed.. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]. End state, read-only.
ctx.seed: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]. Start state, read-only.
ctx.changes: ({ ignore?: entity[], includeJobs?: boolean }?) => { entity, id, kind, fields, origin }[]. Every row created, updated or deleted since seed, over all entities. Excludes engine fields (updated_at) and, by default, changes made by jobs. Use it for collateral checks.
ctx.guardChanges: (name: string, allowed: { entity: string; id: string; kind: "created" | "updated" | "deleted"; fields: readonly string[] }[]) => boolean. Hard collateral guard over ctx.changes(): every change must match an exact entity, row id and kind, and every changed field must be explicitly allowed for that match. No wildcards. An empty list permits no changes. Engine fields and job changes are excluded, as in ctx.changes(). A failed guard makes the grade 0 even if the grader returns 1. Declare target fields and legitimate side effects separately; use ctx.trace() guards for history, including edits later undone.
ctx.trace: () => { seq, method, path, status, routeId, at, body, writes }[]. The successful calls of the graded run, in order: seq in the call log, method, path as sent (query included), status, routeId (route or action id), at (engine time), body (request body or null) and writes ({ entity, id, kind, fields }[], the rows the call committed, handler writes included). Refused calls and jobs are left out. Empty on the untouched seed. Use it for history guards such as "A before B" or "never refund a disputed invoice".
ctx.goal: (weight: number, name: string, ok: unknown) => boolean. Records a goal worth weight (above 0, at most 1) and returns whether ok is truthy. The weights of all goals should sum to 1.
ctx.guard: (name: string, ok: unknown) => boolean. Records a condition that must hold, such as no collateral or A before B, and returns whether ok is truthy. Any failed guard makes the score 0, whatever the grader returns.
ctx.score: () => number. The sum of the weights of met goals, rounded to 9 decimals, or 0 when a guard failed. Return it: guards, then goals, then return ctx.score().
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
```

### client

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.api: (method, path, body?) => { status, body }. Calls the public API through the same path as HTTP. The only way in.
ctx.assert: (condition, message) => void. Fails the test with message when condition is falsy.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
```

### test

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.advance: (duration) => { jobsFired: string[], jobsFailed: { job, at, message }[] }. Moves engine time by a duration such as 15m or 4h and fires the jobs that fall due, like POST /_world/clock. Tests only: task solutions and decoys cannot move time.
ctx.api: (method, path, body?) => { status, body }. Calls the public API through the same path as HTTP. The only way in.
ctx.assert: (condition, message) => void. Fails the test with message when condition is falsy.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
```

input.software: Stripe Billing-style subscription billing (customers, plans, subscriptions, invoices, card payments, and smart-retry dunning)
input.summary: A subscription billing system. Customers hold card payment methods and subscribe to plans. Each billing period produces an invoice that is charged to the customer's default card. A failed charge puts the subscription in past_due and starts dunning. The invoice is retried 1, 3 and 7 days after the first failure. If the 7-day retry also fails, the invoice becomes uncollectible and the subscription is cancelled. Agents can subscribe customers, switch their default card, collect invoices manually, change plans and cancel subscriptions. Hourly jobs renew subscriptions and run the dunning retries. Card outcomes are deterministic: each payment method carries a test token that decides whether charges succeed or how they fail.

entities.name: plan
entities.purpose: A priced subscription offering. Billed every month (30 days) or year (365 days) in USD. Inactive plans cannot take new subscriptions or plan changes.

entities.name: customer
entities.purpose: A billing account holder. default_payment_method_id is the card charged for every invoice. It is readonly and set only by the set_default_payment_method action.

entities.name: payment_method
entities.purpose: A card on file for a customer. The token field is a deterministic test token: tok_visa always succeeds, tok_chargeDeclined fails with card_declined, tok_insufficient_funds fails with insufficient_funds, tok_expired_card fails with expired_card.

entities.name: subscription
entities.purpose: A customer's recurring purchase of a plan. Lifecycle active, past_due, canceled. Holds the current billing period. Readonly fields, changed only by actions and jobs.

entities.name: invoice
entities.purpose: A charge for one billing period. Also holds the dunning state: attempt_count (1 to 4 failed or total charge attempts), dunning_started_at, next_retry_at, last_failure_code. Status open, paid, void or uncollectible.

entities.name: payment
entities.purpose: One card charge attempt against an invoice, successful or failed. Failed attempts are kept as history.

entities.name: billing_event
entities.purpose: Append-only audit trail for a subscription: created, renewed, payment_failed, payment_succeeded, retry_scheduled, past_due, reactivated, plan_changed, canceled. Written by actions and jobs.

About 25% of cards use a failing token (a mix of tok_insufficient_funds, tok_expired_card and tok_chargeDeclined). Of the cards that are default for a customer with an active subscription, all use tok_visa. Subscriptions: 90, with roughly 55% active, 31% past_due (28 rows, so lists page past 25) and 14% canceled (a mix of requested and dunning_exhausted). The 28 past_due subscriptions sit at dunning stages attempt_count 1 (10), 2 (9) and 3 (9). Each has one open invoice with a consistent dunning_started_at, a future next_retry_at (1d, 3d or 7d after dunning_started_at) and a failure code. Four of the attempt_count 3 rows are on the Business plan, spread across list pages, and the others are on Starter or Pro. Active subscriptions have periods ending 1 to 29 days after the clock start. Invoices: paid history for each active subscription (1 to 6 invoices), one open invoice per past_due subscription, void or uncollectible invoices for canceled subscriptions. Payments: one succeeded payment per paid invoice and failed payments matching each past_due invoice's attempt_count. Named anchors: customers 'Harbor Dental' (active Pro subscription, cancel target) and 'Harbor Dentistry' (similar name, active subscription). 'Bluefin Labs' (past_due at attempt_count 1, failing default card, plus a second tok_visa card ending 4444 on file but not default). Events are derived from the invoices and payments in time order.

assumptions.decision: clock.start is 2026-10-06T09:00:00.000Z with tick 0s. All seeded history precedes it. All next_retry_at and current_period_end values in the seed are after it.
assumptions.why: Time moves only on explicit advance, so dunning tests can assert exact timestamps.

assumptions.decision: Retry days (1, 3, 7) are counted from the first failed charge (dunning_started_at). That gives four attempts: day 0, 1, 3 and 7.
assumptions.why: Stripe-style smart retries offset from the original failure.

assumptions.decision: If the day-7 retry fails, the invoice becomes uncollectible and the subscription is canceled with cancel_reason dunning_exhausted.
assumptions.why: A distinct reason lets agents tell it from a customer-requested cancel.

assumptions.decision: Retries and renewals run in hourly jobs.
assumptions.why: Hourly granularity is realistic and deterministic.

assumptions.decision: Card outcomes are deterministic through the test token on each payment_method.
The retry job charges whichever card is the customer's default at retry time.
assumptions.why: Mirrors real dunning and gives agents a fix action.

assumptions.decision: Manual pay_invoice failures are recorded as kind manual and do not change attempt_count or next_retry_at.
assumptions.why: Manual collection must not accelerate cancellation.

assumptions.decision: A failed first charge at subscribe time still creates the subscription (past_due, invoice open) and answers 201.
assumptions.why: A single past_due state keeps the lifecycle small.

assumptions.decision: A month is 30 days and a year is 365 days. Renewal periods are measured from the previous period end.
assumptions.why: Time helpers support only d/h/m/s offsets.

assumptions.decision: USD only, integer cents, no tax, proration, coupons, trials or line items.
Plan changes take effect on the next invoice with no proration.
Cancellation is always immediate, voids an open invoice, and paid invoices stay paid.
assumptions.why: Dunning needs a clear terminal state.

assumptions.decision: A customer cannot hold two non-canceled subscriptions to the same plan (409 duplicate_subscription).
The default card is changed only through set_default_payment_method.
assumptions.why: Forces the explicit step dunning recovery depends on.

assumptions.decision: Failed pay_invoice charges answer 200 with the failed payment.
assumptions.why: A declined card is business data that must persist.

assumptions.decision: List endpoints use the default envelope: data and next_cursor. Errors use {error:{code,message}}.

The default_card workflow gets lifecycle representation descriptive, because its states are derived from whether customer.default_payment_method_id is set and are not stored in a state field. Nothing else in the world changes and all seed counts stay as they are.
assumptions.why: The change request asks for this plan-only revision.

outOfScope.what: Real card networks, 3-D Secure, card tokenisation and PCI concerns
outOfScope.why: Outcomes are simulated by a test token so the world stays deterministic.

outOfScope.what: Taxes, discounts, coupons, credits, proration and multi-line invoices
outOfScope.why: Not part of the requested dunning flow.

outOfScope.what: Free trials, paused subscriptions, cancel_at_period_end and subscription reactivation after cancellation
outOfScope.why: They would add states beyond the three-state lifecycle.
No money moves back in this flow.

outOfScope.what: Customer-facing emails, webhooks and payment-failed notifications
outOfScope.why: Agents act through the API. billing_event stands in for notifications.
Billing records are kept for audit.
The 1, 3 and 7 day schedule is fixed.

open_questions.question: Are the retry days 1, 3 and 7 measured from the first failure, or from the previous retry?
open_questions.default_answer: From the first failure. Retries happen on day 1, day 3 and day 7.

open_questions.question: What happens to the subscription when the last retry fails?
open_questions.default_answer: Cancelled outright, with cancel_reason dunning_exhausted. The invoice becomes uncollectible.

open_questions.question: Should the subscription stay active while dunning runs, or become past_due?
open_questions.default_answer: It becomes past_due on the first failed charge and returns to active on any successful payment.

open_questions.question: Does a manual payment attempt count as a dunning attempt?
open_questions.default_answer: No. Manual attempts are recorded but do not change attempt_count or the retry schedule.

open_questions.question: Should the default_card workflow's derived states be a stored state field on customer?
open_questions.default_answer: No. Declare a descriptive lifecycle on the workflow and change nothing in the world.

workflows.name: subscription_lifecycle
rules: subscribe: the customer must exist and have a default payment method (or the named payment_method_id, which belongs to the customer and becomes default). The plan must be active. The customer must not already have a non-canceled subscription to the same plan (409 duplicate_subscription). Missing card gives 409 no_payment_method. Inactive plan gives 409 plan_inactive.

subscribe creates the subscription with period [now, now + 30d or 365d), creates invoice number INV-<seq> for the plan amount, charges it at once (kind initial) and logs a created event. It answers 201 with the subscription even when the charge fails.
First charge succeeds: subscription active, invoice paid. First charge fails: subscription past_due, invoice open, dunning starts.

Renewal (job): an active subscription whose current_period_end <= now gets a new invoice for the current plan amount covering [old end, old end + interval). The period advances at once. The charge uses kind renewal. Failure moves the subscription to past_due. Past_due and canceled subscriptions are never renewed.
A successful payment of the open invoice of a past_due subscription (retry or manual) moves it back to active and logs reactivated. The billing period is unchanged.

cancel_subscription: allowed from active and past_due only (409 invalid_state otherwise). Sets status canceled, canceled_at, cancel_reason requested. Any open invoice becomes void, with next_retry_at cleared. Paid invoices stay paid.
Dunning exhaustion cancels with cancel_reason dunning_exhausted.

change_plan: not for canceled subscriptions (409 invalid_state). The new plan must be active (409 plan_inactive) and different (409 no_change). Only plan_id changes. The current invoice is not touched and the new amount applies from the next renewal. No proration.

workflows.name: invoice_dunning
rules: Invoice transitions: open to paid, void or uncollectible. All other states are final.
attempt_count counts charge attempts made by the invoice flow (initial or renewal, then retries). Manual payments never change it.
First failed charge: attempt_count 1, dunning_started_at = failure time, next_retry_at = dunning_started_at + 1d, last_failure_code set, subscription past_due.

Retry job, every hour: for open invoices of past_due subscriptions with attempt_count between 1 and 3 and next_retry_at <= now, charge the customer's current default card (kind retry). If the customer has no usable default card the attempt fails with no_payment_method.
Retry succeeds: invoice paid with paid_at, next_retry_at cleared, subscription active.

Retry fails: attempt_count increases. The 2nd attempt sets next_retry_at = dunning_started_at + 3d. The 3rd sets dunning_started_at + 7d. If the 4th attempt (the 7-day retry) fails, the invoice becomes uncollectible, next_retry_at is cleared and the subscription is cancelled with cancel_reason dunning_exhausted.
Retry days are measured from the first failure, not from the previous retry.

pay_invoice: only open invoices (409 invoice_not_open). Optional payment_method_id must belong to the invoice's customer and be active (409 payment_method_mismatch). Otherwise the default card is used. With no card, 409 no_payment_method. A declined manual charge answers 200 with the failed payment, records it with kind manual, and leaves attempt_count and next_retry_at unchanged. A successful one pays the invoice and reactivates a past_due subscription.

workflows.name: default_card

lifecycle.reason: The states no_default and has_default are derived from whether customer.default_payment_method_id is set. They are not stored in a state field, and the customer entity has no state column.

rules: set_default_payment_method takes payment_method_id. The card must belong to the customer (409 payment_method_mismatch) and be active (409 payment_method_inactive). Unknown customer path gives 404 not_found.
The retry job always charges the card that is default at retry time, so replacing a declined default card before the next retry lets dunning recover the invoice.
This is a conceptual workflow. It is not a state field. The customer entity has no state column.

jobs.name: billing_cycle
jobs.rule: Renew active subscriptions whose current_period_end <= now: create the next invoice at the current plan amount, advance the period from the old end (not from now), charge the default card (kind renewal), log renewed and payment events. On failure start dunning and mark the subscription past_due. Skip past_due and canceled subscriptions.

jobs.name: dunning_retry
jobs.rule: Retry open invoices of past_due subscriptions with attempt_count 1 to 3 and next_retry_at <= now against the customer's current default card. On success pay the invoice and reactivate the subscription. On failure bump attempt_count and schedule the next retry at dunning_started_at + 3d then + 7d. When the 4th attempt fails, mark the invoice uncollectible and cancel the subscription with reason dunning_exhausted. Log payment_failed, retry_scheduled, canceled, payment_succeeded and reactivated events.

acceptanceTests.intent: Subscribing with a good card creates an active subscription and a paid first invoice with one succeeded payment.
acceptanceTests.description: A customer with a tok_visa default card subscribes to a 4900 monthly plan. The subscription is active with a 30-day period, the invoice is paid and one succeeded initial payment exists.

acceptanceTests.intent: A declined first charge leaves the subscription past_due with an open invoice and a retry scheduled for 1 day later.
acceptanceTests.description: A customer whose only card fails with insufficient_funds subscribes. The call still answers 201. The subscription is past_due, the invoice is open with attempt_count 1, next_retry_at one day out and a failed payment on record.

acceptanceTests.intent: With a card that keeps failing, retries happen 1, 3 and 7 days after the first failure, then the invoice is uncollectible and the subscription cancelled.
acceptanceTests.description: No retry fires early. After 25h the second attempt runs and the next retry is day 3. After 3d1h the third runs and the next retry is day 7. After 7d1h the fourth attempt fails and the subscription is cancelled with dunning_exhausted. Nothing more is charged afterwards.

acceptanceTests.intent: Replacing the failing default card before the next retry lets the retry succeed, paying the invoice and reactivating the subscription.
acceptanceTests.description: The first charge fails. The customer gets a good card as default. After the day 1 retry fires, the invoice is paid with attempt_count 2, the subscription is active again and the payments are one failed then one succeeded retry.

acceptanceTests.intent: pay_invoice charges an open invoice now. A decline is recorded without touching the dunning schedule, and a success pays the invoice and reactivates the subscription.
acceptanceTests.description: A past_due invoice is paid manually first with the failing default card (200 with a failed payment, dunning unchanged), then with a named good card (invoice paid, subscription active). Paying again answers 409 invoice_not_open.

acceptanceTests.intent: Cancelling a past_due subscription voids its open invoice and stops all retries. Cancelling twice is refused.
acceptanceTests.description: After a failed first charge the subscription is cancelled. It becomes canceled with cancel_reason requested, the open invoice is void, and 8 days later no retry payments exist. A second cancel answers 409 invalid_state.

acceptanceTests.intent: An active subscription is renewed when its period ends: a new invoice for the next period is created and charged, and the period advances by one interval.
acceptanceTests.description: After 31 days a 30-day subscription has a second paid invoice. Its period starts where the first ended and the subscription period now ends on 2026-12-05. A renewal against a failing card moves the subscription to past_due.

acceptanceTests.intent: change_plan switches the plan immediately without touching the current invoice. The new price shows up on the next renewal invoice.
acceptanceTests.description: A subscriber on a 900 plan moves to a 4900 plan. The first invoice stays 900 and the renewal invoice is 4900. Same plan, inactive plan and cancelled subscriptions are refused.

acceptanceTests.intent: Subscribing and setting a default card refuse bad input with clear errors and write nothing.
acceptanceTests.description: Unknown customer or plan answers 400 input.invalid. No card gives 409 no_payment_method. An inactive plan gives 409 plan_inactive. A duplicate active subscription to the same plan gives 409 duplicate_subscription. Setting another customer's card as default gives 409 payment_method_mismatch, and an unknown customer gives 404.
